title: Serbia’s Experiment: Combining Democracy & Meritocracy | NOEMA
gist: Nathan Gardels argues that Serbia's youth-led 'Student List' — which won an absolute majority (53.69%, 140 of 250 seats) after the Novi Sad canopy collapse sparked revolt against Vučić — has installed a meritocratic, non-career-politician parliament, a governance innovation from the democratic periphery that mature democracies' consultative citizens' assemblies have never matched.

insights.claim: Serbia's 14-year rule by Aleksandr Vučić, an autocrat in the mold of Hungary's Viktor Orbán, was challenged by a youth revolt sparked by the November 2024 Novi Sad train-station canopy collapse that killed 16 people and was blamed on corruption in permits and inspections.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A single visible corruption failure can catalyze systemic political change; watch emblematic local disasters as regime-risk triggers in hybrid autocracies.

insights.claim: Gardels links Serbia's uprising to the Gen Z revolts in South Asia: in both, a local issue emblematic of a rotten regime became the spark for a systemic challenge.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Treat Gen Z protest waves as a cross-country pattern of political-risk repricing, not isolated events.
insights.quote: a local issue emblematic of a rotten regime became the spark for systemic challenge
insights.locator: Like the Gen Z revolts in South Asia

insights.claim: Serbia's Student List won an absolute majority of 53.69% in last October's parliamentary elections, taking 140 of the 250 seats, an outcome Vuk Jeremić called a political earthquake that virtually nobody saw coming.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A surprise anti-incumbent supermajority signals a regime shift in Serbia; reassess Serbian political-risk assumptions built on Vučić-era continuity.
insights.locator: They won by an absolute majority

insights.claim: Serbia's Student List is organized as a decentralized, leaderless, horizontal movement that makes decisions, including candidate nominations, through deliberative plenums, and its nomination rules strictly prohibited career politicians.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A leaderless model limits capture but raises execution risk; governance stability is the open question.
insights.locator: The Student List itself is organized

insights.claim: Instead of running themselves, Serbia's student rebels nominated experienced experts (cardiologists, chemists, astrophysicists, a former National Bank of Serbia governor, and the engineer who exposed the Novi Sad corruption), and more than half of the new MPs hold post-graduate degrees.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A technocrat-heavy legislature, including an ex-central-bank governor, points toward institutional and anti-corruption reform credibility.
insights.locator: Among others, the List chose a top economist

insights.claim: The Student List's legislative program focuses on depoliticizing public institutions, restoring judicial independence, eradicating corruption via audits and public-procurement transparency, and restoring academic autonomy with more science funding.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Procurement transparency and judicial independence are the levers that matter for foreign investors and contractors in Serbia; track implementation.

insights.claim: Gardels argues the Student List has turned Serbia's parliament from a platform of patronage into a meritorious citizens' assembly, rarely seen in history: a popular uprising installing a meritocracy in power.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A live test of merit-based democratic governance; its success or failure will be cited in debates over democratic reform.
insights.quote: a popular uprising has installed a meritocracy in power
insights.locator: In effect, the Student List movement

insights.claim: Former Serbian foreign minister Vuk Jeremić cautioned that, given the long shadow of Vučić's rule, translating the Student List's win into competent, stable governance will be a formidable challenge, and its MPs pledged to serve only a transitional term.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Execution and transition risk is high; a self-limiting, inexperienced government could stall or face entrenched-network pushback.
insights.quote: translating this extraordinary achievement into competent, stable and responsible governance will be a formidable challenge

insights.claim: Gardels argues democratic governance innovation tends to come from fledgling states like Serbia (sovereign only since 2006) rather than mature democracies bound by legacy structures and entrenched constituencies.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Look to young or peripheral states for institutional experiments that may later diffuse to the core.
insights.quote: innovation tends also to arrive not from the mature states, but the fledgling ones
insights.locator: It is no less true for being a cliché

insights.claim: Citizens' assemblies in Ireland (abortion), France (climate after the Yellow Jacket protests) and the EU's consultative role for the Commission have never given civil society binding power to act, unlike Serbia's Student List.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Older democracies facing institutional decay and loss of trust may be pushed toward binding civic-governance models; watch for copycats.
insights.locator: There has been experimentation with deliberative polling
